caption: A Palace finite-element simulation of the first-generation SQUAT (the device of Magoon et al.) on sapphire: about 530,000 second-order tetrahedra and 750,000 unknowns. Shown is a cut 0.25 µm above the metal (simplified from 124,000 to 40,000 triangles for the browser), with the electric-field energy density for the left island at 1 V and everything else grounded. The energy crowds into the gap between the islands and along every metal edge, which is exactly where the mesh is finest. The junction itself is drawn schematically, so these are model values. Hover to read values.
readout: island–island 12.0 fF · island–ground 29.9 / 25.4 fF · island–feedline 0.7 / 5.3 fF → model EC/h ≈ 710 MHz
